arxiv-2205-07886.title: An Empirical Investigation of Representation Learning for Imitation
arxiv-2205-07886.creator: Xin Chen, Sam Toyer, Cody Wild, Scott Emmons, Ian Fischer, Kuang-Huei Lee, Neel Alex, Steven Wang, Ping Luo, Stuart Russell, Pieter Abbeel, Rohin Shah
arxiv-2205-07886.description: Abstract Imitation learning often needs a large demonstration set in order to handle the full range of situations that an agent might find itself in during deployment. However, collecting expert demonstrations can be expensive. Recent work in vision, reinforcement learning, and NLP has shown that auxiliary representation learning objectives can reduce the need for large amounts of expensive, task-specific data.

arxiv-2301-12139.title: Bipol: Multi-axes Evaluation of Bias with Explainability in Benchmark Datasets
arxiv-2301-12139.creator: Tosin Adewumi*, Isabella Södergren, Lama Alkhaled, Sana Sabah Sabry, Foteini Liwicki, Marcus Liwicki, firstname.lastname@ltu.se, isasde-5@student.ltu.se
arxiv-2301-12139.description: Abstract We investigate five English NLP benchmark datasets (on the superGLUE leaderboard) and two Swedish datasets for bias, along multiple axes. The datasets are the following: Boolean Question (Boolq) , CommitmentBank (CB) , Winograd Schema Challenge (WSC) , Winogender diagnostic (AXg) , Recognising Textual Entailment (RTE) , Swedish CB , and SWEDN.

arxiv-2403-09956.title: On the distribution of isometric log-ratio transformation under extra-multinomial count data
arxiv-2403-09956.creator: Noora Kartiosuo, Joni Virta, Jaakko Nevalainen, Olli Raitakari, Kari Auranen
arxiv-2403-09956.description: Abstract Compositional data can be mapped from the simplex to the Euclidean space through the isometric log-ratio (ilr) transformation. When the underlying counts follow a multinomial distribution, the distribution of the ensuing ilr coordinates has been shown to be asymptotically multivariate normal.

arxiv-2410-18244.title: Nested active regions anchor the heliospheric current sheet and stall the reversal of the coronal magnetic field
arxiv-2410-18244.creator: A. J. Finley
arxiv-2410-18244.description: Abstract Context. During the solar cycle, the Sun’s magnetic field polarity reverses due to the emergence, cancellation, and advection of magnetic flux towards the rotational poles. Flux emergence events occasionally cluster together, although it is unclear if this is due to the underlying solar dynamo or simply by chance. Aims.

pmc-11288641.description: Mental health in the UK had deteriorated compared with pre-pandemic trends. pmc-11401947.description: Thallium, a highly toxic pollutant, shows greater toxicity to human than other common heavy metals such as mercury, lead, cadmium and its effective removal from wastewater gains great attention. pmc-11654015.title: Effect of a multicomponent exercise program focused on multivariable fatigue improvement versus standard care for glenohumeral instability: MoveUS study protocol
pmc-11654015.creator: Laura Ramírez-Pérez, Antonio Ignacio Cuesta-Vargas
pmc-11654015.description: BackgroundGlenohumeral instability is a highly prevalent pathology; however, there are problems in defining it. Traditionally, structural problems such as labral injury or bone loss in the glenoid cavity and/or humeral side were considered the main causes; but recently, it has been seen that motor control plays a very relevant role.

pmc-12420000.title: Marriage Reluctance Among Tunisian Women: Myth or Reality?
pmc-12420000.creator: D Mezri, M T Ajili, A Gharbia, U Ouali, A Aissa, R Jomli
pmc-12420000.description: IntroductionIn recent years, Tunisia has observed a notable decrease in marriage rates, with a 36% drop in marriage contracts. This decline has been linked to post-independence reforms, modernization, the influence of tourism, media, foreign languages, rapid communication, and international migration, which have transformed values and behaviors related to marriage and family.

pmc-12654416.title: Improve Intermetal Dielectric Process for HTRB Stability in Power GaN High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT) by unbiased-Highly Accelerated Stress Testing (uHAST)
pmc-12654416.creator: Yu-Ting Chuang, Niall Tumilty, Tian-Li Wu, Wei Liu, Kun Wang
pmc-12654416.description: This study investigates a severe high-temperature reverse bias (HTRB) failure observed in GaN HEMTs, with devices failing in under 24 h. We conducted an in-depth analysis of the electrical and physical failure mechanisms, revealing that unbiased-highly accelerated stress testing (uHAST) can effectively induce dielectric delamination.

pmc-12669575.title: Incidence and prevalence of mucous membrane pemphigoid with ocular involvement: a retrospective analysis using the TriNetX database
pmc-12669575.creator: Camellia Edalat, Matthew Spangler, Jennifer Thorne, Paulina Liberman, Meghan Berkenstock
pmc-12669575.description: BackgroundMucous membrane pemphigoid with ocular involvement (oMMP) is an autoimmune disease that results in chronic conjunctivitis, conjunctival scarring, and if left untreated, permanent vision loss. oMMP is quite rare with incidence rates between one in 12,000 to one in 60,000, but there is a lack of large population-based studies that focus solely on oMMP.

pmc-12748920.title: A scalable and long-cycle-life 600 Wh kg−1 solid-state lithium metal pouch cell

pmc-12748920.description: Emerging applications, such as electric aircraft and ships, demand rechargeable batteries with high specific energy. Even with Li metal batteries, achieving a high cell-level specific energy (e.g. ≥600 Wh kg−1) remains a significant challenge.

pmc-12812809.creator: Oluwafemi Ogundarea
pmc-12812809.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background:Colorectal adenocarcinoma (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with variable patient outcomes despite treatment advances. Traditional prognostic methods based on clinicopathological variables alone do not fully capture the biological complexity of the disease.

pmc-12983619.title: Prescriber adherence to treatment guidelines for monoclonal antibodies against Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide in migraine prophylaxis – a register-based cohort study
pmc-12983619.creator: Sofia Nordenmalm, Rickard E Malmström, Sara Freyland, A Ingela M Nilsson Remahl, Karin Wirdefeldt, Isabella Ekheden
pmc-12983619.description: BackgroundCalcitonin Gene-Related Peptide targeting monoclonal antibodies (CGRP mAbs) were introduced for migraine prophylaxis in Sweden through the National Joint Introduction process to ensure an equal, cost-effective, and appropriate national use. This study aimed to assess prescriber adherence to treatment guidelines and evaluate patient treatment persistence during the national introduction of CGRP mAbs.
